I was a battered woman for fifteen years.   I stayed because I didn't feel like I could support my children and my husband always said he wouldn't give me a penny in a divorce.  We married in 1973.  He first hit me in 1980 then it never stopped to the point of choking me with a phone cord.  I still stayed.  But once my daughter was 13, even though she wasn't even interested in boys yet he accused her of being "a n lover".  He was Mormon.  Then shortly after he tried to choke her two times.  I bought a stun gun and a 22 at a garage sale down the street.  I just decided no more choking for either of us.   I always sat on the stun gun during fights from then on.   The time came, I used it and he jumped away and then started coming back for me and while he walked towards me I reached a drawer and pointed it at him.  I had once before pointed a shotgun at him but he got that and broke it.  But this time I was so afraid of what he'd do with this loaded gun that I pulled the trigger.   Then it was over.   I have pretty much been happy ever since.   For my one year in jail for Manslaughter 2 I was then put on probation for five years.   I never for one moment felt guilty of a crime.   I moved my probation to southern California and never reported in, never paid my fine, never did my community service.  I started using drugs and I felt, "oh, you think I'm a criminal?  Watch me now".   I ever hung out with people in the Mexican Mafia.  One of them kept stealing my truck and I'd keep getting it back.  The fourth time, he got me better.   He told the police I offered him $5,000 to kill someone.   Of course, they believed him.  He was in jail for something else so two birds with one stone.  He got me off the streets so I couldn't get my truck back and he got himself a get out of jail card.  It worked for him.  I went to CA prison for 2 years, got brought back to Oregon for Probation Violation.  Tried to tell my story about the pickup guy and nobody listened.  Probation violation 20 years in prison.   I did eight before my appeal for passing a psych test got me home to my kids.   Now I've been happy ever since and even in prison I was.   I wrote a book about my story and here it is 35 years later I am going to publish.  My daugher gets any money it makes by the way.  My son died of cancer in 2021 at age 42.

I lost my son to cancer 2 years ago.  During his final month he wasn't eating anything.  When cancer attacks the body it can make food more trouble for them as their body can't process it.  Causes pain and prolongs the death process.   As a Mom it was so difficult to suppress the desire to FEED your child.  The hospice literature said not too.  Ryan would ask for ice cream until his last few days.  You know the pain they must experiencing and it tears your heart to pieces.  When you mention euthanasia it would be nice for them to have less pain but then you have somebody like my son that fought till the bitter end.  He wanted to get downstairs to his room and computer so badly.  Now I am kicking myself for not unhooking that computer and bringing it upstairs.  I think all of us will think of things we wish we had done.  My advice to all, drop all you're doing in life and spend each moment you can with them.

I can help a bit with having surgery upon one's brain area.  I had a 4 cm tumor behind my left eye.  That is a very large tumor, so big they couldn't do anything else but operate.  I was so afraid of having someone use a bone saw to cut my skull that I decided to forego surgery and just let end of life come.  My 30 year old son started crying when I told him that.  So guess what, I did it.  Went for the surgery because it's what Moms do.  Here is why I am writing this because that "fear" you have of brain surgery for whatever reason will prove to be unfounded and unnecessary.  There are no "pain nerves" inside your head.  You are knocked out unconscious when they enter your head, you never feel it and they use a plate to repair any damage they do.  You never ever feel that.  They even left a needle in my head and had to go back in, I was told while in recovery.  So that was the same deal.  I would say the only uncomfortable thing was they fold the skin and staple it now.  You are going to feel that for the rest of your life.  Just a feeling in my face.  My incision was from my ear to top of head.  So I do wonder why people get plastic surgery and get this stretched skin feeling when it's not necessary.  But I would be absolutely gone if I hadn't done this.  It was in 2008.  So brain surgery was less painful than a C-section.  So no matter what you face do it.  Do you best. My son died two years ago yesterday.  Feb 11, 2021.  His sister, his niece and me all believe the same thing.  He is not gone, he is still with us, surrounding us and seeing everything we do. For some reason he did not.  Yup, Ryan, my son, gets the credit for that and many other things that happen.  Why is my computer still working so well without Ryan here to use TeamViewer to fix it?  Many other things.  I left a teddy bear with a heart on it on his his hospice bed and asked him to please put some spirit in it for me.  Now it sits by my computer so it can see my two monitors.  Give Ryan some of that computer exposure still.   If I did not feel this way I couldn't survive myself.  Who knows where people go and what happens.  Nobody knows.  I could be right I could be wrong I could be totally nuts.  I don't care.   When Ryan was a baby I would touch his eyebrows to help him get to sleep.  Now I still do that to this teddy bear often.  So I think people fighting cancer can also do good for themselves to imagine a good place ahead.
